The only column that differs categorically is `source.ip`, which `environment_notes` lists as an unstable identifier in playground-v2 (container addresses reassigned per lever-up), so it cannot evidence a delta; user.name, auth_method, and failed=0 are all baseline-identical, and accepted 5 vs 6 is not a categorical distinction. The other controls do not overturn this: C-7d has `window_live: false` (not measured), and C-21d is live but empty, which only fails to corroborate rather than contradicting C-14d. No surfaced field distinguishes the observed rows from baseline rows, so this reads as additional but indistinguishable activity, not `present`.

Two live control windows (C-14d at 2026-07-11 and C-21d at 2026-07-04, both `window_live: true`) returned the identical shape: row_count 0, empty `values`, same columns (failed/source.ip/user.name). l-003.evidence: The lead contains a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with params `{host: db-1}`, and the observed payload carries only `_note: state lookup` plus the echoed params — no event rows, no `@timestamp` field. The `baseline` array is empty because, per `environment_notes.state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries carry no `@timestamp` bounds to move and therefore have no control window; that empty baseline is not a missing measurement. With one CMDB entity-record query and no event stream, there is nothing to diff, so the lead is tagged `state-only` regardless of row content. Only one query is decidable, so `heterogeneous` is null.
